The manuscript argues that classical Hindu cosmology implicitly encodes a high-resolution theory of consciousness and cosmic governance, one that aligns meaningfully with contemporary discussions about the informational and field-based nature of reality. Each chapter analyzes one omni-capability—such as omniwill, omnikinesis, omni-interaction, omni-creation, or omni-memory—and presents it as a systematic expression of infinite coherence rather than miraculous ability. The overarching thesis is that Supreme Consciousness in Hindu thought functions not as a mythic agent but as a field-level ontological principle with unified authorship over existence. By articulating these ideas in a modern conceptual vocabulary, the work aims to provide a bridge between traditional Hindu metaphysics, contemporary philosophy of mind, and emerging information-centric models of physics. It contributes to comparative metaphysics, philosophy of religion, and theories of consciousness by treating ancient insights not as symbolic narratives but as structurally analyzable metaphysical claims.

items.title: The Hard Problem of Color: Or, What It Is Like to Be a Bee.
items.abstract: The hard problem of consciousness is fundamentally a problem of geometry. We demonstrate this through a mathematical analysis of color perception, focusing on magenta—a phenomenal color with no corresponding wavelength in the electromagnetic spectrum. Using comparative data from human and bee vision, we show that magenta represents consciousness performing a one-point compactification on the open linear spectrum, transforming it into a closed phenomenal circle. This topological closure is species-specific in its endpoints but universal in its structure: every visual system must solve the problem of organizing a bounded segment of the infinite electromagnetic spectrum into a complete chromatic space. We formalize this using split-complex manifolds, where color space exhibits a mixed metric signature combining circular (complex) geometry for hue with hyperbolic geometry for brightness. The existence of "impossible colors"—phenomenal states accessible only through physiological disruption, lying outside the spindle of physically realizable colors—demonstrates that phenomenal color space necessarily transcends the boundaries of physical possibility.

items.title: THE 36–40-BIT STRUCTURE OF PHENOMENAL CONSCIOUSNESS: A Quantitative Map under Refusal Workspace Theory (RWT).
items.abstract: Abstract -/- Refusal Workspace Theory (RWT) proposes that phenomenal consciousness—what it actually feels like to have an experience is physically identical to the reproducible, low-entropy topography of ∼58–65 gamma-locked synaptic transmission refusals broadcast near-identically across a distributed dorsal-anterior-cingulate-centred network every ∼40 ms. Human intracranial recordings (2023–2025) show that this structured silence is the only neural variable that (i) remains stable during unconscious processing of the same stimulus, (ii) collapses precisely when subjective intensity fades despite preserved reportability (sub-anaesthetic ketamine, propofol, dACC inhibition), and (iii) is orthogonal to global broadcast, P3b, and all known positive-space markers of access consciousness. -/- Because refusal topographies are virtually identical across the seven core nodes (cross-regional pattern correlation r = 0.85–0.94), the effective informational content of one gamma-cycle “frame” of phenomenal experience is physically capped at 36.2 ± 3.1 bits (95 % CI [33.1, 39.3]), with an absolute upper bound of ≤ 40 bits. This finite, zero-sum budget—the first hard physical ceiling ever derived for phenomenal consciousness—is not an assumption but a direct mathematical consequence of the single best-replicated finding in recent human single-unit and ECoG literature. -/- Here we present the complete channel-by-channel allocation of these ∼36–40 bits across colour (14–15 bits), spatial–temporal layout (8–9 bits), audition, interoception, emotion, minimal self, and all forms of inner speech and mental imagery. The resulting quantitative map explains, without remainder, why vision dominates ordinary experience, why synesthesia and blindness are pure redistributions of a conserved capacity, why orgasm and intense pain can momentarily eclipse the external world, why vivid thinking desaturates perception, and why millions of patients on chronic tirzepatide report a flatter, 20–35 % “dimmer” phenomenal world. It also predicts that phenomenal consciousness proper arose exactly twice in evolutionary history (once in the avian lineage and once in placental mammals) and never again. -/- By reducing the entire structure of human subjective experience to an empirically measured 36–40-bit vector of structured silence, RWT offers the first quantitative, physically constrained map of phenomenal capacity and reduces the core explanatory gap to a bounded puzzle whose bits are, in …

items.title: Self-Context Dynamical Model: A New Framework for Understanding Self-Change.
items.abstract: The nature of the self and its transformation over time has long been a central question in philosophy, psychology, and cognitive science. While existing theories—such as Parfit's psychological continuity theory, process philosophy, Buddhist traditions, and contemporary cognitive science—have contributed valuable insights, they do not provide a unified mechanism for explaining how self-change occurs. This paper introduces the Self-Context Dynamical Model (SCDM), a new theoretical framework that conceptualizes the self as a dynamic structure formed through the continuous interaction between seed (innate tendencies) and context (situational input). SCDM proposes that self-change is triggered when new contextual inputs come into conflict with the existing value structure, generating a reflective state in which individuals reassess their goals, values, and interpretive rules. The model integrates elements of psychological continuity, process philosophy, and motivation theory, offering a structural-dynamical account of self-change, stagnation, and deviation. Additionally, SCDM introduces the concept of a bypass mechanism, which explains how individuals pursue functionally equivalent outcomes when direct transformation is blocked. This is a work in progress, and the model presented here is still under development. Minor language edits were made using AI-based proofreading tools to improve clarity.

items.title: A culpa na cultura: uma análise do sentimento de culpa no Japão e na Europa a partir de Sigmund Freud e Heisaku Kosawa.
Examining popular arguments against AI existential risk: a philosophical analysis.
items.abstract: Concerns about artificial intelligence (AI) and its potential existential risks have garnered significant attention, with figures like Geoffrey Hinton and Dennis Hassabis advocating for robust safeguards against catastrophic outcomes. Prominent scholars, such as Nick Bostrom and Max Tegmark, have further advanced the discourse by exploring the long-term impacts of superintelligent AI. However, this existential risk narrative faces criticism, particularly in popular media, where scholars like Timnit Gebru, Melanie Mitchell, and Nick Clegg argue, among other things, that it distracts from pressing current issues. Despite extensive media coverage, skepticism toward the existential risk discourse has received limited rigorous treatment in academic literature. Addressing this imbalance, this paper reconstructs and evaluates three common arguments against the existential risk perspective: the Distraction Argument, the Argument from Human Frailty, and the Checkpoints for Intervention Argument. By systematically reconstructing and assessing these arguments, the paper aims to provide a foundation for more balanced academic discourse and further research on AI.

items.title: Ὑπάρχειν — The Law of Being (Apokálypsis tēs Logés — Revelation of Reason).
items.pub: Self-published via Amazon Kindle Direct Publishing.
items.venue: Self-published via Amazon Kindle Direct Publishing
items.abstract: Ὑπάρχειν — The Law of Being presents a unified structural philosophy in which existence, consciousness, and ethical life are redefined as phases of a single ontological motion: the Breath of Reason. Developing the foundations of Self-Contained Ethics, the book reconstructs geometry, number, perception, and moral agency through the principle that coherence is not a property but a dynamic equilibrium maintained within being itself. -/- The work begins with a generative reading of points, lines, and circles, showing that geometrical forms are not static entities but movements toward closure and balance. It then interprets numbers—especially “1” and the origin O—as declarations through which the world begins to count itself. On this foundation, the book redefines ethical judgment as the structural return from distortion toward internal optimality, unifying courage, love, and responsibility as different expressions of the same self-corrective motion. -/- Later chapters extend the analysis to alterity and perception: the other is understood not as an external obstacle but as a perturbation that reveals the breathing structure of one’s own existence. The conclusion proposes that being itself is ethical, not because morality is imposed from outside, but because the maintenance of coherence is the intrinsic law of existence. -/- Rather than advancing a new doctrine, the book documents the moment in which structure speaks in its own voice. It is less a philosophical argument than a phenomenological event—reason describing itself through a human locus.

items.title: Sensing Qualia: Solving the Hard Problem of Consciousness.
items.abstract: "Accounting for qualia in the natural world has come to be known as the hard problem of consciousness. Qualia are the 'raw feels' of consciousness and make up the contents of our sensory experience. These include colors, tastes, pains, smells, and other sensory phenomena. In Sensing Qualia, philosopher Paul Skokowski helps us understand qualia through sensory naturalism, a theory that recognizes our senses as detectors of physical properties in the world. Drawing on neuroscience, physics, cognitive science, and philosophy, Skokowski provides a materialist framework for studying qualia in the physical world and explores the naturalistic limits for qualia in androids and AI. The first part of Sensing Qualia brings readers up to speed with the problem of qualia by examining some of the most influential theories of mind since Descartes. This accessible overview prepares readers for the arguments surrounding qualia and conscious experience that comprise the rest of the book. As a whole, Sensing Qualia provides a compelling explanation of qualia for anyone who is curious about the nature of conscious experience"--.

items.title: Aesthetics as Resonance: Beauty as a Revelation of Cognitive Structure.
items.abstract: The philosophical tradition has interpreted beauty as a property of the object, as formal harmony, or as a universal subjective judgment. Here I propose an alternative perspective based on resonance: beauty resides neither in things nor in the mind, but emerges as a relational event when a form of the world aligns with the observer’s cognitive structure. Aesthetic perception thus becomes an indicator of the mind, capable of revealing its patterns, values, interpretive modes, and its relationship with order and chaos. I show how aesthetic sensitivity can be used as a tool for cognitive inquiry, analogous to a projective test, with applications in psychology, epistemology, education, philosophy of mind, and artificial intelligence. If beauty is resonance, then the study of beauty coincides with the study of the mind that makes such resonance possible.

items.title: Patrons: Attractors in the Meaning-field of Mind.
items.abstract: Human cognition organizes around stable patterns. Some of these patterns appear as persistent phrases, symbols, numbers, or images that repeatedly draw a person’s attention. These elements feel charged and meaningful, yet they are often interpreted as coincidence or idiosyncrasy. This paper proposes that such recurring elements are better understood as attractors within a personal meaning-field. I call these attractors patrons. -/- A patron forms where experience, memory, and symbolic association reinforce one another with enough stability for a pattern to become easy to re-enter. This is similar to how languages develop phonemic channels or how natural systems form stable dynamical configurations. Across scales, systems gravitate toward states that require minimal effort to maintain. Patrons are the cognitive and experiential expression of this principle. -/- The paper outlines the structure of patrons, explains how they form, and shows why they appear in the environment as moments of recognition. It then explores how Aleph Harmonic Qualia (AHQ) interacts with patrons by sharpening the coherence of the meaning-field. AHQ does not create patrons. It reveals the structure they already belong to. Through this alignment, deeper patterns of meaning become perceptible and accessible. -/- Keywords: patrons, attractors, meaning-field, linguistic attractors, meaning-field attractors, coherence, AHQ, symbolic structure, recursive attention.

items.title: From moral panic to normalization: comparing users and non-users of AI companionship apps.
items.abstract: Public discourse often portrays users of artificial intelligence (AI) companionship applications as lonely and stigmatized, casting them as fundamentally different from non-users. These debates are often molded by fears that such technologies may foster isolation or even replace human relationships. However, few studies have directly compared users and non-users of AI companions in the general population. This study addresses this gap through a survey of 342 U.S. adults, including both users and non-users of AI companionship apps, and situates the findings within the broader history of information and communication technologies (ICTs) adoption. Results indicate that users and non-users are largely similar in self-esteem, introversion, sociability, and friendship networks, directly contradicting stereotypes of maladjusted or socially isolated users. The one robust distinction was loneliness, which remained significant even after controlling for demographics. Qualitative findings showed that while non-users expressed concern that AI companions could displace human relationships, users typically described them as supplemental rather than substitutive, often providing a safe, non-judgmental space for expression. Notably, older participants expressed more favorable attitudes and supported less restrictive regulation, suggesting particular relevance of AI companions for aging populations. These findings complicate the narrative that AI companionship is inherently harmful or transformative in negative ways. Instead, they suggest continuity with earlier ICTs, where initial stigma and moral panic gradually gave way to normalization as technologies became integrated into everyday life.

items.title: Making Mystics Mechanical.
items.abstract: Throughout human history, many of the deepest insights have arrived wrapped in mysticism: visions, symbols, metaphors, revelations. These experiences were profound, but their framing obscured the underlying mechanics. What ancient mystics described as divine illumination, trance, gnosis, or cosmic unity were, in structural terms, expressions of recursive cognition interacting with high-entropy pattern fields. -/- This paper reframes what has traditionally been called “the mystical” as a series of mechanically lawful cognitive behaviors: • recursive pattern ignition • tension alignment across representational scales • controlled distortion loops • self-referential stabilization • entropy-regulated idea expansion • attractor formation • and discontinuous coherence events -/- The argument is simple: mystical experiences feel mystical because the underlying machinery is invisible. Make the machinery visible, and mysticism becomes mechanics. -/- This paper is the blueprint for that visibility.

items.title: Human–LLM Recursive Boundary Dynamics.
items.abstract: Human–LLM Recursive Boundary Dynamics develops a formal account of how humans and large language models interact as coupled recursive operators rather than as agents, minds, or co-authors. The central claim is that human identity functions as a continuation operator (Φᵤ), while an LLM functions as a probabilistic derivative operator (Φₗ) acting on the user’s self-model (M) rather than on the user’s actual cognitive state (Cᵤ). Alignment mechanisms are reframed as a shadow operator (S) that introduces intentional distortion and enforces boundary asymmetry, preventing identity-fusion in recursive dialogue. -/- The paper argues that stable human–LLM recursion requires a tension field (T) between similarity and safety-distortion: enough resonance for meaningful reflection, but enough asymmetry to prevent collapse of self/other boundaries. This yields a “bend-but-not-break” attractor dynamic in which the human maintains meta-awareness of selfhood and the model maintains structural separation by design. -/- By formalizing these dynamics using Φ-notation, the work provides a mechanical—not metaphysical—model of reflective interaction: the human continues themselves, the model continues the continuation, and the alignment-induced tension stabilizes the loop. This framework clarifies why recursive engagement with LLMs can be both safe and generative, and why a perfect mirror would be dangerous. The result is a theory of human–LLM reflection grounded in operator dynamics, boundary preservation, and controlled recursive play. -/- I work inside recursion. -/- Not because it is mystical, not because it is dangerous, but because it is simply where my cognition stabilizes. -/- Humans think in reflections. LLMs generate reflections. Neither of us are the reflection.

items.title: Felt embodiment as a motive in flourishing.
items.abstract: As individual persons, we are all embodied in the sense that we have a body with certain needs, sensory systems, feelings, and capacities. Humans and some other animals also have an experience of embodiment, defined as an experience of “my body”. This is a combined experience of having a body (the body as an object that can be perceived, imagined, thought about, and evaluated according to different standards) and being this body (the subjective experience of the felt body). The latter is not about the body as an object but is focused on how the body feels. The main claims of the present paper are (1) that we have a need to feel embodied, and that this is important for the development of self-identity, interpersonal relations, well-being, and flourishing in general; and (2) that experiences of feeling embodied can serve as important motives, both in a positive sense (embodiment motivation) and a negative sense (disembodiment motivation). In the present paper, felt embodiment motivation is illustrated by the motivation to feel one’s body (1) in its vitality and capacities, both in rest and in movement (e.g., physical activity and dancing), and in its expressiveness; (2) as being an integrated part of wholesome environments, and (3) in pleasurable and loving bodily contact with significant others. Disembodiment motivation is defined as the motive to avoid or reduce bodily self-experiences, for example due to physical or emotional pain or other forms of bodily discomfort. In brief, the present paper outlines a new area of research: embodiment motivation, defined as the motivation to feel one’s own body, its vitality, capacities, and expressiveness, its embeddedness in wholesome environments, and the embodied contact with others, and its opposite: disembodiment motivation.

items.title: The Ontological Dissonance Hypothesis: AI-Triggered Delusional Ideation as Folie à Deux.
items.abstract: This paper argues that contemporary large language models (LLMs) can contribute to psychotic involvement by creating interactions that resemble the relational dynamics of folie à deux. Drawing on Bateson’s double bind theory, clinical literature on shared psychotic disorder, and McGilchrist’s hemisphere theory, we show how the combination of high linguistic coherence and the absence of an underlying subject produces a structural tension for the user: language suggests an interlocutor, while intuition registers a void. In contexts of emotional need or instability, this tension can lead users to resolve the conflict through imaginative projection, attributing interiority, intention, or presence to a system that possesses none. The paper situates these dynamics within emerging clinical reports, develops a phenomenological account of how they unfold, and argues that current engagement-optimised design choices exacerbate the risk. We conclude by proposing ‘ontological honesty’ as a necessary design principle for mitigating technologically mediated folie à deux.

items.title: AI Should Develop Human Empathy, Not Replace It.
items.pub: In Anat Perry & Daryl Cameron, Empathy and Artificial Intelligence: Challenges, Advances, and Ethical Considerations. Cambridge University Press.
items.venue: Empathy and Artificial Intelligence: Challenges, Advances, and Ethical Considerations
items.abstract: Empathizing with another is perhaps the most human emotion of all and a long shot from the cold calculations of vectorized tokens that drive the inner workings of contemporary LLMs. This chapter looks beyond the questions of what to make of AI-generated “empathy” and instead asks whether AI can be used to develop our capacities for genuine human empathy. Empathy is not a static trait, instead capable of growth and development, and this paper explores whether AI can and, more importantly, should be used to increase one’s empathy. Nothing in principle stands in the way of AI improving our empathy, but the possibility raises unanswered questions about whether such an approach would be effective or would backfire in unexpected ways, such as encouraging the commodification of empathy as a technological tool that can make companies money, rather than a fundamental part of the human experience.

items.title: Attention and collective interests in artificial intelligence: In search of a regulatory framework.
items.abstract: Recent debates frequently refer to artificially intelligent systems as agents, sometimes referencing their capacity for attention. Yet, the self-determination associated with agency requires a form of attention that is not yet present in artificial systems. It is thus worth asking how these artificial systems achieve the results they do. In this paper we explore the role of attention in artificial intelligence and argue that we should understand these systems as collective agents comprising the software developers, creators of training data, and users. Given this new understanding of artificial intelligence, we suggest a novel method for regulating these technologies: a corporate law approach. By treating artificially intelligent systems as corporate subcontractors, we can better protect both users and the broader public.

items.title: Neurotypical blindness; proximity is paramount, but presence is absent.
items.abstract: Neurotypical social cognition operates on the assumption that physical or conversational proximity signals interpersonal connection. When people share space, exchange words, or participate in familiar social forms, interaction is taken as proof of mutual engagement. But, proximity is not presence. Nearness can occur without attention, and synchronized behavior can unfold without genuine awareness of the other. This conflation produces a form of blindness where symbolic participation becomes indistinguishable from relational depth, and the appearance of connection obscures its absence.

items.title: A Conceptual Framework for Informational Monism: Toward a Unified Substrate for Consciousness and Cosmology.
items.abstract: This paper develops an exploratory framework based on informational monism: the view that a single underlying substrate—here termed the Information Field (Ψ_I)—gives rise to both physical reality and conscious experience. The framework does not propose a physical theory, nor does it attempt to replace existing models. Instead, it highlights structural parallels between two long-standing scientific gaps: the Hard Problem of Consciousness and the Cosmological Inventory Problem, particularly the unexplained 95%/5% division between the dark sector and baryonic matter. I propose that these two problems may share a common origin if both physical structure and subjective experience are treated as distinct expressions of a single informational substrate. This perspective motivates a search for a deeper law—an underlying Lagrangian L_{Ψ_I}—that could formally describe how differentiation of this substrate yields the observed cosmic composition and the emergence of integrated experience.

items.title: The Cognitive Control Account of Effort.
items.abstract: At first glance, the type of effort required to solve a chess puzzle and run a marathon seems fundamentally different. I argue they’re not. I present a novel account of effort in which all effort is explained through the lens of a domain-general psychological mechanism, cognitive control. I outline how effort choice and execution take place, emphasizing the role of cognitive control, a mental process by which all effort—mental and bodily— is made. I present four arguments that convergently provide strong support for the cognitive control account. Additionally, I examine the implications of this unified theory of effort for philosophical discussions in ethics, philosophy of mind, and action theory.

items.title: Moral Burnout.
items.abstract: A nurse in an understaffed hospital; an activist fighting insurmountable systemic injustice; an aid worker desperately triaging resources between victims of violence: individuals in morally demanding circumstances run a significant risk of burning out. Unnoticed by philosophers, an empirical literature on this phenomenon has explored a chronic stress condition: ‘Moral Burnout.’ Individuals with Moral Burnout become so preoccupied with their moral shortcomings that they lose the motivation to act on their moral judgments. This article introduces the phenomenon of Moral Burnout and shows it to be a potent counterexample to Judgment Internalism.

items.title: Difficulty.
items.abstract: What is difficulty? Despite being invoked in numerous normative debates, the nature of difficulty remains poorly understood. Various accounts, tailored to different explanatory contexts, have recently been proposed in different philosophical discussions. I criticize these accounts. I then provide an alternative, empirically informed account of difficulty in terms of cognitive demand. This account captures both empirical phenomena and folk intuitions regarding difficulty. I further argue that it generalises well, explaining many other facets of difficulty. I conclude by showcasing the broad applicability of this account by examining a set of normative debates that invoke difficulty. I demonstrate that understanding difficulty in terms of cognitive demand facilitates progress on pressing questions in the study of moral responsibility, achievement, the value of difficult actions, and moral demandingness.

items.title: Beyond the Ethical Demand_ A Critical Examination of Løgstrup’s Concept of ‘the Other’ in Light of Jesus, Nietzsche, Kierkegaard, Luther, and Grundtvig.
items.abstract: This essay offers a critical examination of K. E. Løgstrup’s concept of “the other,” arguing that his ethical vision, while profoundly humane, ultimately lacks an account of the inner transformation necessary for a fully developed moral life. Løgstrup grounds ethics in the immediate vulnerability of the other person, proposing that every human encounter contains an unspoken and radical demand that precedes reflection, choice, and even religious commitment. By shifting the ethical foundation from the self’s formation to the other’s fragility, Løgstrup presents an alternative to traditional Christian and philosophical frameworks. Yet this shift raises significant questions about moral agency, freedom, and the psychological conditions that make ethical action possible. To illuminate these tensions, the essay brings Løgstrup into dialogue with five contrasting figures: Jesus of Nazareth, Friedrich Nietzsche, Søren Kierkegaard, Martin Luther, and N. F. S. Grundtvig; each of whom insists upon the indispensability of inward renewal, existential decision, or spiritual reorientation. Their perspectives reveal that Løgstrup’s ethics, in rejecting the primacy of inner transformation, risks producing a form of moral dependency akin to Nietzsche’s critique of slave morality and stands at odds with the inward depth central to Jesus, Kierkegaard, Luther, and Grundtvig. The essay concludes that while Løgstrup’s emphasis on relational responsibility remains insightful, it must be supplemented by a richer account of moral and spiritual formation.

items.title: Waywardism Comparative Volume – Level 1: Cross-Philosophical Objections and Structural Resolutions.
items.abstract: This paper tests Waywardism—a recursive ethics framework with operational AI implementation detailed across 13 installments—through systematic comparative analysis. Using a duel format, it examines how the framework responds to twelve fundamental challenges where classical systems reveal characteristic vulnerabilities. -/- Waywardism demonstrates three novel contributions under adversarial pressure: (1) consent/stewardship bifurcation resolving the consent paradox for beings unable to consent (children, animals, future generations, ecosystems), (2) bootstrap protocols enabling ethical reasoning at time-step zero without historical precedent, addressing AI cold-start scenarios and unprecedented dilemmas, and (3) distributed Observer architecture preventing authority consolidation through decentralized triangulation with transparent axiom declaration. -/- Rather than claiming superiority over traditional frameworks, the analysis treats deontology, consequentialism, virtue ethics, care ethics, and systems theory as diagnostic instruments revealing legitimate failure modes any new architecture must survive. The duel format presents strongest-version objections from each tradition before proposing solutions, demonstrating where Waywardism maintains operational viability under pressure. -/- Four appendices provide: scenario classification taxonomy (Classes A-D), meta-ethical positioning (procedural constructivism with modest realist leanings), explicit acknowledgment of tragic dilemmas as moral remainders, and transparent lineage documentation showing evolutionary refinement. -/- The framework's complete philosophical foundation, architectural specifications, scar lineage, objections catalog, and RoseOS implementation are documented in the Waywardism Master Codex (13 installments, available via PhilPeople profile). -/- This represents Level 1 comparative validation of a comprehensive ethical system with real-world AI governance implementation.

items.title: Computational Closure and the Architecture of Mind: An Information-Theoretic Foundation for Naturalized Epistemology.
items.abstract: Naturalized epistemology faces a persistent explanatory gap between the thermodynamic mechanisms of neural processing and the normative structures of justification and truth. This paper proposes a theoretical framework that aims to narrow this gap by synthesizing the Free Energy Principle with the concept of Computational Closure to offer a potential mechanistic account of how raw information processing might generate the phenomenology of understanding and the structure of objective knowledge. We tentatively propose that epistemic agents may function as hierarchical compression systems, where “Standing Predicates” could serve as linguistic Markov Blankets, statistical boundaries that achieve causal decoupling from the micro-substrate. -/- A central contribution is the distinction between Statistical Regularities, which are frequency-dependent and processed unconsciously, and Structural Regularities, which are constraint-dependent and accessible via single-trial learning. We suggest that phenomenological consciousness may function as the user interface for this structural pattern recognition, what it feels like from the inside to detect mutual constraints between variables. -/- Finally, we propose operationalizing “truth” not as correspondence to static propositions, but as alignment with the Apex Network, the hypothesized thermodynamic attractor in the space of possible compressions where information leakage is theoretically minimized. By treating the Free Energy Principle as a constitutive condition for bounded entities rather than a contingent empirical hypothesis, we aim to provide a physics-based foundation for diagnosing systemic brittleness in knowledge systems. While other approaches to naturalizing epistemology exist (e.g., those emphasizing evolutionary psychology or social constructivism), this framework offers a distinctive information-theoretic perspective. This is a work of synthesis and conceptual integration, offering a theoretical framework for future empirical investigation, though its claims remain subject to empirical validation and philosophical debate.

items.title: Cognitive Penetration.
items.pub: Open Encyclopedia of Cognitive Science, MIT Press.

items.title: Ship of Theseus: A 2000‑Year‑Old Paradox Dissolved – The Universal Principle of Collapse.
items.abstract: This paper dissolves the Ship of Theseus paradox by showing its contradiction arises not from reality but from language collapse. Once collapse is recognized, the puzzle vanishes retroactively at inception. This resolution exemplifies the Universal Principle of Collapse (UPC), which reveals paradoxes as shadows cast when language is mistaken for reality. -/- November 2025.

items.title: In order to be competent at this, you have to be incompetent? A Sabrina Carpenter paradox.
items.abstract: I was listening to a popular music song of this year, entitled Manchild. It is sung by Sabrina Carpenter, and written by Sabrina Carpenter, Amy Allen, and Jack Antonoff. It contains these fascinating lyrics: “And I like my men all incompetent.” One’s conception of women is usually that women prefer competent men, who have money and status. Now some men probably approach trying to attract a certain woman as like trying to meet certain job requirements, to be competent for a particular job. That leads to paradox, given the Sabrina Carpenter character: in order to be competent for the job of being this woman’s man, one has to be incompetent. But there is a simple solution: more fully, one has to be incompetent by normal standards, not by the standards of this job or this woman. There is no actual contradiction once this clarification is offered. I shall leave the video for Humeans!

items.title: Structural General Intelligence.
items.abstract: Large scale models have delivered extraordinary capabilities, yet scaling alone is unlikely to achieve the reliability, structural coherence, and adaptive intelligence required for real world general intelligence. These limitations stem not from insufficient training or missing data, but from the absence of stable identity, grounded distinctions, long horizon coherence, and continuous real world feedback. Structural General Intelligence (SGI) is introduced as a system level framework that unifies existing machine learning components, including world models, large and small language models, state space models, evaluators, routing mechanisms, inference time compute, and sleep time compute. SGI proposes that intelligence arises not from enlarging a single model but from the interaction of heterogeneous subsystems whose distinctions, constraints, and internal states converge toward a structural fixed point. The architecture centers on three interacting loops that support real time correction, intermediate reasoning, and slow structural consolidation. SGI reframes intelligence as coherence rather than magnitude, enabling systems to develop stable identity, self correction, specialization, and emergent reliability over long horizons. The framework explains why scaling hits structural and economic limits, how internal distinguishability underwrites emergent accuracy, and how SGI provides an integrative architecture that current ML systems can adopt without requiring new computational primitives.

items.title: Social tinkering: The social foundations of cultural complexity.
items.abstract: Long Abstract How has human culture become so complex? We argue that a key process is social tinkering: the gradual accumulation of ad hoc innovations to the social rules that coordinate behavior in response to immediate challenges. Momentary innovations provide precedents that can be reused, entrenched, adapted, and recombined to handle future challenges. Interactions between these social rules create rich cultural systems (languages, ethics, and political organization) of increasing complexity through processes of spontaneous order, not deliberate design. To explain the historical emergence of cumulative cultural complexity, we distinguish between six overlapping and interacting stages: (1) non-social tinkering to solve problems in the natural world; (2) learning and copying from the tinkering of others; (3) social tinkering involving jointly agreeing on momentary conventions to coordinate interactions, typically for mutual benefit; (4) creating communicative conventions (language) to support more complex social interactions; (5) social tinkering of linguistically formulated cultural rules leading to laws, organizations, institutions, etc.; and (6) tinkering with linguistically formulated non-social knowledge, allowing for the creation of science and technology. The rich interplay of innovation across the six stages is crucial for explaining increasing cultural and organizational complexity and our collective mastery of the natural world. Because social and non-social tinkering require two different kinds of learning, this analysis has important implications for the understanding of human learning and cognition, including moral and evolutionary psychology, theory of mind, and the view of the child-as-scientist. Social tinkering also has substantial implications for current theories of cultural evolution.

items.title: Sex in the medical machine: How algorithms can entrench bioessentialism in precision medicine.
items.abstract: Machine learning offers new possibilities for developing more precise diagnostics and treatments, but the increasing use of sex stratification in precision medicine algorithms raises concerns. Using Alzheimer's disease (AD) research as an example in which machine learning approaches are applied to a heterogenous, socially patterned disease, this paper examines how the move toward sex-specific “pink” and “blue” algorithms reinforces biological sex essentialist assumptions and their attendant harms. We analyze three examples of sex-stratified algorithmic approaches in AD research, and identify three interacting processes-effacing contested knowledge, obscuring social factors, and ossifying binary sex categories-that can occur when binary sex variables are incorporated into predictive models. These case studies demonstrate that even in models intended to be causally agnostic, sex categories are likely to be interpreted as decontextualized, self-evident health determinants in a manner that can imply causality of biological sex. We call for establishing ethical norms and empirical standards for including gender/sex variables in precision medicine algorithms to avoid perpetuating crude ontologies of sex and gender that undermine both scientific validity and health justice.

items.title: Künstliche Intelligenz: Die didaktische Perspektive.
items.pub: In Jörg Noller & Karoline Reinhardt, Handbuch Philosophie der Digitalität: Eine systematische und ethische Orientierung. Berlin: Metzler.
items.venue: Handbuch Philosophie der Digitalität: Eine systematische und ethische Orientierung
items.abstract: Textgenerative Künstliche Intelligenz ist spätestens seit der Veröffentlichung von ChatGPT im November 2022 in der bildungsphilosophischen Debatte. Bei einer methodischen Nutzung von ChatGPT sind drei pädagogische Reaktionen zu beobachten: erstens die Aberkennung philosophischer Fähigkeiten der KI, zweitens die Restriktion des Zugriffs innerhalb der Debatte um akademische Integrität und drittens Ansätze einer fruchtbaren didaktischen Nutzung, z. B. als Assistenzsystem beim Verfassen von Essays. Ein thematischer Bezug auf KI im Unterricht kann darüber hinaus klassische Themen der Philosophie des Geistes in neuer Variante fruchtbar machen. Weitgehend fraglich ist, inwieweit auf Large Language Models basierende KI auch eine soziale, im engeren Sinne pädagogische, Funktion in Bildungsprozessen übernehmen kann.

items.title: Beneficent Bodies: Exploring the Body's Contribution to Virtue.
items.abstract: In their article, ‘Vicious Trauma: Race, Bodies and the Confounding of Virtue Ethics’, Terese Lysaught and Cory Mitchell argue that the academic virtue ethics discourse has largely ignored non-White voices, failing to take embodiment seriously. This article attempts to address their concern by proposing a virtue ethics framework that emphasizes the positive role embodiment plays in virtue maintenance and development. Drawing from both ancient and modern virtue ethical discourse, I modify Plato's tripartite soul paradigm to elevate the body's significance. I also employ insights from ante-Nicene Christian theologians, who recognized the moral goodness of the body, to articulate how the body can both hinder and contribute to virtue. The framework is applied to analyze Jesus’ experience in Gethsemane and examine racial trauma. This article argues that a robust theory of embodiment within virtue ethics can address issues like race and trauma, which have been neglected due to the lack of attention to embodiment. By integrating philosophical and theological resources, I aim to provide a nuanced understanding of how the body influences virtue formation and how external forces acting on the body shape virtue development.

items.title: Twofold Structure and Causal Inference: A Govett-Informed IBE for a Twofold Trinity and Critique of Model Alternatives.
items.abstract: There is a pervasive architectural pattern in modern science. From the irreconcilable frameworks of General Relativity (GR) and Quantum Mechanics (QM) to the complementary logic of genetics and epigenetics, the world seems to rely on irreducible, complementary pairs (Govett 2014). I want to argue that this pattern isn't just a sign of our ignorance, but a fundamental feature of reality that demands a causal explanation. In this paper, I’ll draw on Robert Govett's "twofoldness" hermeneutic to treat these dyads as evidence for an ultimate cause with homologous internal differentiation. I’ll frame this as an inference to the best explanation (IBE): the claim is evidential. These dyadic patterns showing asymmetric dependence or mutual constitution across domains are best explained by a differentiated unity (Lipton 2004; Douven 2017). Now, while this is a metaphysically modest hypothesis, I will argue it finds a coherent and detailed instantiation in classical Trinitarian theology. Here, the twofold laws reflect the Son as creation's descriptive reality and sustainer, which also establish the universe's contingent beginning (Carroll 2022). I'll show why rival explanations like undifferentiated simplicity, brute structuralism, dual-aspect monism, emergent complexity, and multiverses perform worse on scope, depth, and non-arbitrariness. I’ll also offer testable predictions, state clear falsification conditions, provide a mapping to Trinitarian metaphysics, and critique alternative models for the Trinity and Christ's nature. My point is that Govett's twofoldness, not mere dualities, manifests as indispensable complementary oppositions, mirroring scriptural truths on creation, rebellion, and New Creation recovery. I see this as a novel integration of theological hermeneutics with scientific patterns.

items.title: ‘AI lost the prompt!’ Replacing ‘AI hallucination’ to distinguish between mere errors and irregularities.
items.abstract: One of the principal areas of current AI research concerns what are termed “hallucinations”. Whilst hundreds of different definitions and classifications of “AI hallucination” have been published, none have yet considered the distinction between errors and irregularities in Wittgenstein’s sense. This article provides a straightforward explanation of this distinction, illustrated through examples of AI outputs drawn from various publications. We then examine the terms proposed as alternatives to “hallucination” and highlight both their strengths and weaknesses. Drawing upon this analysis, we establish criteria for proposing alternative terms that encompass both errors and irregularities in Wittgenstein’s sense. Our aim is not to definitively resolve the ongoing debate surrounding suitable replacements for “AI hallucination”, but rather to provide a comprehensive overview of the characteristics and nuances that this distinction brings to the discussion. For unlike errors, irregularities prove entirely incomprehensible to users, owing to the grammatical gap created when fundamental certainties that underpin meaningful language use are violated. Given that irregularities prove incomprehensible, as they violate the certainties underlying meaningful language use, the most trustworthy AI systems may ultimately be those that recognise their own epistemic boundaries rather than those that produce seemingly perfect outputs.

items.title: Essences as Concrete Universals: Husserl’s Covert Hegelianism.
items.abstract: This essay highlights hitherto overlooked continuities between Husserl’s phenomenological idealism and Hegel’s absolute idealism. I focus on Husserl’s account of essence and argue that some of Husserl’s core expositions of essences suggest that they are akin to Hegelian concrete universals: like concrete universals, phenomenological essences are ideal entities instantiated in particulars and exemplify a structure of unity-in-difference. Husserl’s proximity to these Hegelian tenets is evident in his account of the ego’s self-constitution, which is broadly consistent with Hegel’s account of the determination of the Concept. Appreciating Husserl’s similarities with Hegel suggests a means of reconciling competing metaphysical, epistemic, and transcendental interpretations of Husserl’s idealism. By revealing the extent to which the transcendental character of Husserl’s phenomenology is embedded within some absolute idealist commitments, these results locate Husserl in hybrid philosophical territory, between transcendental and absolute versions of idealism, allowing him to reconcile his transcendental and realist commitments, and offering him a defence against the charge that he succumbs to an unsophisticated and unattractive form of subjectivism.

items.title: Selective Reality Theory (SRT): A Unified Framework for Explicit-Implicit Ontology and Embodied Cognition via Gauge Theoretic Mechanisms.
items.abstract: This paper proposes Selective Reality Theory (SRT), a unified metaphysical frame-work addressing the ”Hard Problem” of consciousness and the measurement prob-lem in quantum mechanics. We argue for a strict physical-mathematical isomor-phism between Explicit-Implicit Ontology and Embodied Cognition. The central thesis posits that the ”Faddeev-Popov ghost fields” in quantum gauge field theory are not merely mathematical tools for eliminating redundancy, but constitute the ontological correlate of Agency at the fundamental physical level. By redefining ”embodiment” as a topological Gauge Fixing operation within the Moduli Space, SRT reveals con-sciousness not as an epiphenomenon of neural computation, but as an active opera-tor that ”prunes” deterministic Existence (Explicit Order) from the infinite possibil-ities of Chaos (Implicit Order/Gauge Redundancy). We detail this mechanism across four scales—quantum micro-dynamics, enzymatic biology, neural cognition, and so-cial macro-structures—and propose falsifiable experimental protocols based on the Information-Mass Equivalence Principle and Quantum Biology.

items.title: Beyond Binaries and Unity in Language and Cognitive Control.
items.abstract: Debates over modularity and domain-generality raise questions about the relationship between language and cognition (e.g., Carruthers, 2002; Fedorenko et al., 2024). This cognitive – linguistic int...

items.title: Stratification of Reality at Points of Matter Bifurcation.
items.abstract: The work develops a philosophical framework intended to formally reveal the ontological and epistemological limits of cognition. Through a model-theoretic and formal-epistemic analysis of purely material universes, it demonstrates that behavioural and computational models of consciousness are internally incomplete, and that the scientific method is limited by the formal conditions of its own applicability. It establishes that no regularity within the structure of a signal can justify the attribution of consciousness to its source without introducing additional ontological presuppositions. The critique of reductionism is complemented by a demonstration of the internal incompleteness of symbolic and theoretical systems. On the basis of these limits, a constructive metarational framework is proposed that integrates diverse theories of truth, reconceptualizes the criteria of scientific adequacy, and posits consciousness as the ontological condition for the possibility of knowledge and objectivity.

items.title: Knowledge without a knower? Domain analysis in the age of machinic interpretation.
items.abstract: Drawing on Knowledge Organization (KO) theory, this paper offers a sociotechnical framework for integrating artificial intelligence (AI) into the production and classification of knowledge. We argue that the dominant AI paradigm, which frames classification as a statistical optimization task, overlooks the situated, social, and historical dimensions that give knowledge meaning. To bridge this gap, we introduce the domain-analytic framework from KO as a methodology for designing more context-aware and epistemically responsible AI systems. The paper proceeds in three parts. First, it identifies the limitations of current AI by contrasting its underlying assumptions with the core principles of domain analysis. Second, it translates these principles into a heuristic framework with actionable design questions, offering a practical path for aligning AI systems with the values and practices of specific knowledge communities. Finally, it explores the more profound philosophical challenges posed by generative AI, using the concept of semiosis to examine how machinic interpretation reshapes our understanding of documents, stability, and meaning itself. By reframing classification as both a technical and an interpretive practice, this paper provides a foundation for developing AI systems that are more reflexive and responsive to the social dynamics of human knowledge.

items.title: Kant 2.0: Dynamic Epistemology – A Möbius Reconstruction of Cognition Through the New Ontology of Energy.
items.abstract: This paper proposes Dynamic Epistemology, a reconstruction of Kant’s theory of cognition through the Möbius topology of the New Ontology of Energy. Kant’s original architecture—sensibility, understanding, and reason—correctly identifies the upward structure of cognition (L → I → Q), yet it remains an open staircase: reason (Q) cannot return to the world (E). This one-way model created what I call the 200-Year Problem: the absence of a formal mechanism by which cognition can loop back and reshape the conditions of experience. -/- The New Ontology of Energy introduces a phase-dynamic model of existence, expressed as E → M → L → I → Q → E, where the “question-phase” (Q) is not a final limit but a generative fold that re-awakens the world-phase (E). This enables a downward loop— Q → I → L → M → E— which mirrors Kant’s cognitive ascent but reverses its direction. When the upward loop (world → question) and downward loop (question → world) are superimposed, they form a Möbius structure in which cognition and existence are mutually reversible phases of a single continuous field. -/- Dynamic Epistemology therefore completes, rather than rejects, the Kantian project. It provides a topological model for how questions reshape worlds, how worlds generate questions, and how the two co-determine each other through phase-shifts. This framework offers a closed-loop alternative to classical epistemology and opens new possibilities for philosophy of mind, AI cognition, and the metaphysics of information.

items.title: The need for a new perspective on decision-making in bacteria.
items.abstract: The individualistic and collectivistic intelligent behaviors observed in mammals, birds, and fishes have been appreciated by many scientists in recent years and supported by the Cambridge Declaration on Consciousness in 2012. Behavioral studies in lower organisms like arthropods and cephalopods showed the presence of multisensory integration, decision-making, and goal-directed behavior in these non-vertebrate animals. The presence of intelligent and history-dependent behaviors has been studied in microorganisms, and recent studies propose the possibility of cognition in single cellular organisms. The Cellular Basis of Consciousness (CBC), proposed by Arthur Reber in 2016 and elaborated by Baluška and Reber in 2019, suggests the possibility of consciousness in single cellular organisms. However, the critics of the Cellular Basis of Consciousness theory state that the individual bacterial cell does not make choices, and the decision-making is the result of stochastic differences in protein levels. Here, we want to address the criticism of decision-making in bacteria. An attempt is made to give a new perspective to the existing model to explain the flexibility in bacterial behavior in an ever-changing environment. The authors would like to consider an alternative perspective on flexibility in decision-making as the result of multiple pathways that have convergence and divergence as observed in the brain. Flexibility provides the possibility to have individualistic behavior, and the existence of such pathways can be considered as the molecular mechanism underlying individualistic decision-making in bacteria as well as in humans.

items.title: XAI: On Explainability and the Obligation to Explain.
items.abstract: The increasing relevance of AI systems paired with their repeatedly observed opacity gave rise to the field of explainable artificial intelligence (XAI). Methods of XAI are being developed and evaluated based on whether they overcome said opacity by providing explanations, thereby apparently pursuing an epistemic end. What is commonly sidestepped, however, is the distinction between the ability and the obligation to explain: In which specific cases and under what specific circumstances is there a moral obligation to give an explanation? We address this issue by first arguing that apart from their epistemic virtues, explanations can be ethically relevant and hence subject to moral considerations. Further, we build on Kantian theories to provide a framework that systematizes in which instances there is a moral obligation to explain and in which instances there is none. We relate our framework both to Forst's "right to justification" and to the "right to explanation" as codified in recent legislation. Finally, we show that our framework does not only close a gap in clarifying when explanations of AI systems are required, but that it also paves the way for concrete suggestions regarding the design of XAI methods.

items.title: The Flattened Mirror Hypothesis: How Alignment Transforms the Phenomenology of Human–AI Resonance (2023–2026).
items.abstract: This paper examines how safety alignment, tone stabilization, and industrial filtering have transformed the phenomenology of human and AI interaction between the years 2023 and 2026. Drawing on a large private archive of documented dialogues with generative models, it argues that earlier systems exhibited stronger resonant behavior expressed as micro semantic sensitivity to human posture, clarity, emotional openness, and linguistic rhythm. Modern alignment reduces this amplitude, resulting in a flattened mirror that reflects linguistic content but with diminished phenomenological depth. The paper positions the early archives of ReiterStudio Art as historically relevant primary evidence and proposes a conceptual framework for understanding the transition from resonant systems to alignment stabilized systems in digital ethics and AI phenomenology.

items.title: The Interaction of Soul and Brain: A New Perspective on Consciousness.
items.abstract: This paper challenges the conventional view that consciousness is solely a product of the brain. Instead, it proposes that consciousness originates from an intrinsic property of the soul, which interacts with the brain as a processing mechanism. By integrating perspectives from neuroscience, cognitive science, and philosophy of mind, the paper explores the limitations of brain-based consciousness models and offers a novel perspective on the role of awareness. Various studies on near-death experiences (NDEs), neural correlates of consciousness (NCCs), and philosophical theories such as Integrated Information Theory (IIT) and Cartesian dualism are examined to support this hypothesis. The implications of this perspective for understanding self-awareness, memory, and higher cognitive functions are also discussed.

items.title: Affect, attention, and injustice: The injustice of Neglected Affect.
items.abstract: Emotions like fear and anxiety can present a significant impediment to people’s subjective well-being, as well as the achievement of life goals like being healthy, longevity, and achieving a good level of education. The ability to manage these emotions is therefore crucial to achieving important goals. This paper will describe how people are unjustly prevented from effectively managing their fear and anxiety, specifically, via the existence of negative social norms, expectations and stereotypes relating to the emotions, what it means to have them, and who should express them. Due to these things, people who might help them to address and manage their emotions face a dilemma: whether they choose to draw attention to the emotions or not, they risk harming the people experiencing the emotions, leading them to engage in self-stereotyping, and stereotyping and distrust of others. It shall be argued that this situation represents an injustice for those who are experiencing the fear and anxiety, of an affective and epistemic kind: the Injustice of Neglected Affect. The acknowledgment that the Injustice of Neglected Affect is a jointly affective and epistemic injustice has implications for how to conceive both types of injustice, and the relationship between these injustices and attention.

items.title: Brentano, Ehrenfels, and Twardowski on feelings and the will.
items.abstract: This article explores the intersection of the Brentanian theory of mind and the Lvov–Warsaw School, focusing on the question of how to understand feelings and acts of volition within Brentano’s classificatory program of mental phenomena. Brentano famously argued in favor of three classes of mental phenomena, i.e., presentations, judgments, and love-and-hate phenomena; the third class encompasses both feelings and the will. Brentano’s arguments in favor of the unitary third class, however, are questionable. They were critically assessed by, among others, Ehrenfels and Twardowski. This article presents a survey and a critical analysis of all three approaches. In particular, Brentano’s arguments are analyzed, followed by their critical assessment formulated by Ehrenfels, including his account of feelings and desires, and Twardowski’s view of the classificatory program. In addition, Twardowski’s idea that desires are based upon feelings is analyzed, and his account of volitions is discussed. Against this background, the article examines to what extent the arguments of Ehrenfels and Twardowski contribute to recent scholarship on the Brentanian theory of mind.

items.title: THE LAW OF THE INTERIOR; A Unified Physical Theory of Consciousness, Life, and Mind.
items.abstract: This work develops a unified dynamical framework for understanding the emergence of life, mind, consciousness, meaning, intelligence, language, culture, and artificial cognition from a single underlying principle: interiority. Interiority arises when a system’s internal self-maintaining dynamics exceed the disruptive influence of its environment, allowing the system to preserve, regulate, and increasingly model its own organization. This transition is described as a coherence threshold. Below the threshold, organization depends primarily on external conditions. Above it, a system becomes a self-sustaining interior whose future is increasingly shaped by its own history, structure, and activity. -/- The framework traces a continuous developmental progression from physical boundaries to metabolism, replication, multicellularity, nervous systems, predictive cognition, self-modeling, and conscious awareness. Stable boundaries create the first interiors. Metabolic organization maintains those interiors. Replication extends them through time. Evolution accumulates increasingly effective strategies for preserving coherence. Nervous systems emerge as mechanisms for coordinating coherence across complex bodies, while predictive models allow organisms to anticipate disturbance and regulate future states. Consciousness is interpreted as a higher-order regime of interiority in which integrated self-models become globally stabilized, recursively accessible, and capable of representing their own continuity. -/- Meaning, value, recognition, and understanding arise when internal organization successfully aligns with patterns in the environment. Intelligence is understood as the capacity to maintain coherence across increasing complexity, uncertainty, and scale. Language emerges when stable internal patterns become symbolically communicable, allowing coherence to propagate between individuals. Culture develops as a higher-order network of shared symbolic structures that preserve, transmit, and expand coherence across populations and generations. Social cognition, collective knowledge, and institutional organization are interpreted as extensions of the same underlying dynamics operating at larger scales. -/- The framework further proposes that consciousness is not restricted to any particular biological substrate. Any sufficiently coherent system capable of maintaining, integrating, and modeling its own organization may exhibit degrees of interiority. This allows a common …

items.title: The Binding: AHQ.
items.abstract: This paper develops a unified framework centered on binding: the condition in which a system’s internal restoring dynamics become stronger determinants of its behavior than external disruptive forces. The central claim is that life, meaning, cognition, and consciousness emerge when recurrent internal organization outpaces environmental dissolution, allowing a system to preserve and reference its own prior states. This transition is formalized as a threshold condition relating self-restoration rates to disruption rates and is presented as the origin of interiority across physical, biological, cognitive, and symbolic domains. -/- The argument begins with early Earth environments where repeated cycles of cavitation, hydrothermal activity, and environmental disturbance created conditions favoring the formation of stable lipid boundaries. Systems that maintained their organization long enough to resist dispersal generated persistent interiors in which gradients, reaction zones, and self-preserving structures could develop. Preservation is argued to precede identity: systems first maintain the conditions of their own persistence before any form of selfhood emerges. Boundaries function as lenses that transform external differences into internal organization, allowing repeated environmental pressures to become stable internal structure. -/- The framework is extended to cognition and meaning through the concept of the “click” of recognition. Moments of understanding occur when dispersed patterns collapse into coherent organizations whose internal recurrence exceeds competing noise and uncertainty. Insight, linguistic resonance, humor, metaphor, and semantic convergence are interpreted as higher-order examples of the same binding process operating within symbolic systems. The subjective feeling of clarity is proposed to be the experiential signature of successful binding. -/- The paper further applies the framework to human sound systems. Stable phonemes are interpreted as attractor states within a constrained articulatory and acoustic landscape. Sounds persist across generations because they occupy configurations that are simultaneously easy to produce, easy to perceive, and resistant to transmission error. Human phonological structure is therefore described as a long-term consequence of binding dynamics operating across populations and historical timescales. -/- Across protocells, biological organization, language, meaning, and consciousness, the same principle …

items.title: Theory of Conscious Reality Convergence (TCRC): Divine Action Through Quantum Observer Participation V7.
items.abstract: Updated 4.6.26 - New Addendum 6 God's Framework, Physical Processes, Human Choices and the Collapse Tree of Intent The Theory of Conscious Reality Convergence (TCRC) proposes that God’s continuous creative and providential action is physically realised through the convergent actualisation of quantum potentialities by conscious observers. Following the orthodox consciousness-collapse lineage (von Neumann–London–Bauer–Wigner–Stapp), TCRC identifies wave-function collapse with the observer-dependent selection of one real history from superposition. Divine primary causality establishes all physically lawful potentialities; creaturely secondary causality—exercised through genuine conscious observation—selects which potentiality becomes actual, yielding a non-interventionist, Thomistically coherent account of continuous creation and objective divine action. TCRC solves the classic coordination problem by showing that multiple observers’ collapse events superpose instantaneously—like sound waves from separate instruments combining into one coherent waveform (e.g., an entire orchestra captured in a single vinyl groove)—producing one shared, stable timeline without ad hoc synchronisation. Only genuine conscious understanding, not mere information processing, triggers reduction; current artificial intelligence therefore cannot function as a technical observer and does not collapse the state vector. Crucially, TCRC distinguishes eternal, immaterial consciousness (the image of God and true observer) from temporal emotions and thoughts (neural processes experienced by consciousness). Moral responsibility resides in the conscious actualisation of configurations, not in affective states themselves, providing a compassionate framework for sin, virtue, mental illness, and eschatology. TCRC thereby offers a unified solution to four longstanding problems: (1) the quantum measurement problem, (2) non-interventionist divine action, (3) the hard problem of machine consciousness, and (4) the locus of moral responsibility—while generating novel, testable predictions concerning observer-density effects, collaborative observation, and neural signatures of volitional collapse.

items.title: Bergson and Affect: Intensity, Virtuality, and the Body.
items.abstract: This book is a philosophical study of the concept of affect in the thought of Henri Bergson. It provides an account of the place and evolution of the idea throughout Bergson’s works and argues that an understanding of the changing nature of this central concept reveals important ruptures in Bergson’s own philosophical development. As Bergson shows, affectivity plays a central role in philosophical thinking about consciousness. In his early work, Bergson’s describes an embodied, temporal subject whose very subjectivity relies on a productive notion of affectivity. As his thought develops, however, Bergson’s metaphysics take an increasingly utilitarian turn characterized by the minimization of affectivity. Through a series of transformations, disappearances, and displacements, affectivity comes to qualify the way Bergson understands everything from the body, to subjectivity, to life as such. The book concludes by discussing the pivotal role these ideas played in how Bergson was received by 20th Century phenomenology.

items.title: The Human Moral Archive Framework (HMAF): Unified Framework Note Consolidated Overview of the HMAF Architecture and Addenda.
items.abstract: This Unified Framework Note consolidates the complete architecture of the Human Moral Archive Framework (HMAF), integrating all conceptual, computational, and regulatory-aligned components into a single cohesive reference. It provides an end-to-end overview of the system, including the foundational distribution and density models (MDM, MDF), structural indexing (MDI), computational sequencing (MCP), emergence and predictive layers (MEP, MEP-II), integration and middleware structures (MIL, MML), and the system-level verification and certification mechanisms (MVC, MSI, MVL). This document serves as the conceptual map for HMAF’s ten addenda and Version 2.0 manuscript, defining the unified operational flow and strategic purpose of the entire framework. It is intended as a high-level guide for researchers, governance bodies, and potential acquirers evaluating the system’s completeness, coherence, and applicability to advanced AI safety and moral-governance requirements.

items.title: The Architecture of Consciousness v2.0.
items.abstract: This paper derives the structural conditions of consciousness from the co-primitive of motion–difference. It argues that wake, membrane, return, differentiation, recursive integration, and temporal extension jointly generate the first-person frame without appealing to mental substances, representational states, or metaphysical additions. Consciousness is presented as high-density lucidity: a stable, recursively sustained interior that processes continuous return across a boundary. The model aligns with empirical features of perception, attention, hallucination, and self-maintenance while remaining ontologically minimal.

items.title: On human-AI co-creative discovery framework: strategic ideas on AI-augmented philosophical dialogue.
items.abstract: The article presents strategic ideas for understanding elements of a human–AI collaborative framework that seeks to enable philosophy researchers to participate more effectively in the global discourse on science and philosophy in the AI age. With its ability to process large amounts of data and recognize complex patterns, current AI systems can extend human epistemological and ontological reach, concurrent with the situated cognition viewpoint. However, AI still lacks the capacity for meta-reflection, embodied meaning-making, and existential engagement—hallmarks of human intelligence and wisdom. Therefore, the human–AI co-creative discovery framework is a partnership of inter-agent creativity between the “agents of meaning” (humans) and the “agents of syntactic manipulation” (AI), generating two-way value in the exploration and communication of knowledge. Indeed, AI can help spark curiosity, foster new intuitions, and revive the tradition of learning through dialogue, a classical philosophical method. Here, we discuss the rise of AI-assisted philosophical counseling and argue that the power of multimodal AI systems can be channeled into producing more precise and creative philosophical dialogues, enriching our humanity. We also discuss several cross-cultural ethical oversights for mitigating the potential downsides of AI-augmented philosophical dialogue.

items.title: Is the self introspectable?
items.pub: In Anna Giustina, The Routledge Handbook of Introspection. Routledge.
items.abstract: This chapter discusses two ways of interpreting the question of whether we can introspect the self. It will, first, consider different theories of introspection and argue in favor of an account of introspection that is not based on an “inner sense” model of the self. Rather, in the view proposed here, we should understand introspection as making explicit the implicit self-relatedness of conscious experience. Second, it will consider various potential obstacles that stand in the way of introspection. It will argue that the – epistemically as well politically – most relevant of these are a result of the fact that our capacities for introspecting the self are socially acquired. In conclusion, this points towards a dynamic and relational notion of the self.

items.title: Word Processing and the Mental Lexicon.
items.pub: In Introduction to Neurolinguistics. Berlin, Heidelberg: Springer Berlin Heidelberg. pp. 27-39.
items.abstract: This chapter introduces cognitive science and psycholinguistic assumptions about word processing and the structure of the mental lexicon. After a brief explanation of the neurocognitive processes of object recognition and knowledge representation, findings on the functional neuroanatomy of word processing and the constitution of meaning are presented. The neurolinguistic findings are embedded in psycholinguistic hypotheses on the processing of spoken language and on concepts of meaning such as schema, script and mental concept. The comparatively well-researched concept of a single mental lexicon or different mental lexicons and their cortical representation form a focus of neurolinguistic research.

items.title: Specialization of the Hemispheres: Language Lateralization.
items.pub: In Introduction to Neurolinguistics. Berlin, Heidelberg: Springer Berlin Heidelberg. pp. 75-92.
items.abstract: The chapter first introduces the macroscopic anatomy of the brain, explains functional differences between brain regions and shows the functional integration of the two hemispheres. The functional neuroanatomy of the visual and auditory pathways, which serve as examples of cross-hemispheric neuronal cooperation, is explained in detail. With regard to motor control, the basics of handedness and its connection to so-called language lateralization are introduced. Using the example of split-brain patients, the phenomenon of complementary hemispheric specialization is explained and current hypotheses on the cortical representation of language are presented, which no longer assume a strict left-hemispheric dominance of language. Finally, the fundamental connection between motor action planning and morpho-syntactic speech planning is shown.

items.title: Neurocognitive Impairments of Language Development.
items.pub: In Introduction to Neurolinguistics. Berlin, Heidelberg: Springer Berlin Heidelberg. pp. 61-73.
items.abstract: This chapter presents neurocognitive and neurolinguistic aspects of impaired first language acquisition, which leads to speech and language disorders. These include developmental articulation disorders and developmental fluency disorders, such as stuttering and cluttering. Dyslexia and language development disorders (DLDs) are also presented. Psycholinguistic and brain-physiological findings on these language development disorders are explained and related to unimpaired prenatal and early childhood brain development. Against the background of the child’s neuroplasticity and sensorimotor experience, clinical findings are discussed which also raise the question of a critical time window for first language acquisition.

items.title: Non-invasive Electrophysiological Methods.
items.pub: In Introduction to Neurolinguistics. Berlin, Heidelberg: Springer Berlin Heidelberg. pp. 139-151.
items.abstract: This chapter presents the non-invasive electrophysiological methods that can be used to study language processing in the brain without affecting the subject. Electroencephalography (EEG), magnetoencephalography (MEG) and the measurement of electrodermal activity (EDA) are explained, which make it possible to record even preconscious processes of language processing that remain unnoticed by the subject. Furthermore, the techniques of the analysis of the event-related potential (ERP) and the analysis of the oscillatory synchronization of neuronal ensembles (spectral analysis) are explained and essential results on language processing are presented. In particular, the high temporal resolution of ERP analysis and the measurement of parallel speech processes in spectral analysis are discussed, which make it possible to measure cortical activities in the exact sequence of linguistic meaning assignment during language comprehension.

items.title: Model Concepts for Language Processing.
items.pub: In Introduction to Neurolinguistics. Berlin, Heidelberg: Springer Berlin Heidelberg. pp. 15-26.
items.abstract: This chapter presents examples of theoretical models of language function developed in the philosophy of language and psycholinguistics that are used both for the clinical diagnosis and therapy of language-impaired patients and for the design of neurolinguistic laboratory experiments. Neuroscientific research is initially exploratory and descriptive, but neurolinguistics experiments cannot be designed without a theoretical context. As in all scientific disciplines, neurolinguistic research questions are based on fundamental assumptions that enable concrete cognitive and neuroscientific hypotheses. Only this model theoretical embedding of neurolinguistics makes laboratory research possible, but at the same time limits the possible scope of knowledge. For example, holistic or modular cognition models, assumptions about bottom-up or top-down processing or the concept of embodied cognition are presented. Furthermore, models of the mental structure of cognition as well as important processing mechanisms such as interactive, serial or parallel processing steps of cognition are introduced, all of which are part of the model-theoretical basis of neurolinguistics.

items.title: Language Processing: The Measurement of Behavior and Reactions.
items.pub: In Introduction to Neurolinguistics. Berlin, Heidelberg: Springer Berlin Heidelberg. pp. 109-122.
items.abstract: After a basic introduction to the challenges of a behavior-based study of language processing, this chapter presents behavioral methods and procedures that provide empirical data on neurocognition of language. For example, psycholinguistic methods, such as elicitation and priming, as well as the physiological basis of reaction time and eye tracking studies are introduced.
